analysis: This PR adds only documentation: a changelog entry (changelog.d/ssd-eviction-selection.md) and a new paragraph in docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (head lines 531-546) plus a date bump on line 3. No executable code is in the supplied evidence. The text describes an SSD eviction change in SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest. It does a linear SSDBlockIndex.oldest probe first. If that file is busy or undeletable, it takes an oldestFirstSnapshot heap and walks it on demand. The ordering stays last hit then tag, and the first tag is excluded. File leases, epoch validation, the removal lock and the reconcile-then-recheck-budget step are described as unchanged. This concerns T-041 (SSD tier at-rest posture, TTL and LRU disk budget) and TB-007. The documented behavior does not touch the HMAC naming, DBK3 crypto, the 30-minute TTL cap, scope salting or KEK purge. No new on-disk metadata or prompt-derived fields are added. It does not raise TTL or retention. Eviction is documented as bounded, so the availability and disk-budget assumptions in T-041 are not weakened by the text. Open question for the next pass: the actual Swift change (SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift, SSDBlockIndex.swift) is not supplied. Whether the snapshot path preserves lease and epoch checks, bounds the busy-file walk, and enforces the disk budget under concurrent eviction cannot be confirmed from this evidence. The doc admits that concurrent schedules may pick different victims from a stale snapshot. That is a behavioral note, not a proven regression. No findings. Source code review is deferred.
